song.title: All Day And All Of The Night

guitar.modelsText: Gibson Flying V / Harmony Meteor / Telecaster
guitar.notes: Dave Davies famously slashed his amp speaker for distortion using a Harmony/Telecaster-type setup; reasonably documented, medium confidence is fair.

tone.target: dirty garage fuzz through small British combo
tone.profile: dirty garage fuzz through small British combo
tone.summary: A high-gain, fuzzy signal chain utilizing a pre-drive (OD 9/Green OD) followed by heavy distortion (Red Haze/Fuzz), paired with a small British amp model (UK 45 or UK 50) and a vintage cabinet to achieve the desired raw, nasal garage sound.

rig.name: The Kinks - All Day And All Of The Night - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray noise from the aggressive fuzz and high gain.
Provide initial compression and a slight boost of bite before the main fuzz stage.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used here to simulate the 'push more bite' correction, acting as a mild compressor/overdrive foundation.

alternatives.reason: A dedicated compressor would be ideal for maximizing sustain and tightness.

blocks.purpose: Generate the core 'nasal fuzz' and raw mono drive required for garage rock.
blocks.gap: The Red Haze is chosen over Fuzz/RAT-style to better capture the specific, slightly buzzy, nasal quality associated with early Kinks records.

alternatives.reason: A general fuzz model could also work but might lack the specific 'nasal' character.

blocks.purpose: Kept inactive to maintain raw signal integrity and focus on pure fuzz tone.
blocks.gap: No specific wah effect was requested or implied by the target sound.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the 'small British combo amp' and provide a raw, punchy foundation.
blocks.gap: The UK 45 is ideal for capturing the small, aggressive sound of early British amps.

alternatives.reason: A close second choice, offering a similar vintage British tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide the necessary 'British speaker' character and tight low end.
Enhance the 'bright top end' and cut unnecessary low-end mud while boosting mid-range bite.
blocks.gap: Used for surgical tone shaping to meet specific frequency requirements (bite, brightness).

alternatives.reason: Could also be used but Guitar EQ 2 offers more precise control needed for this aggressive sound.

blocks.purpose: Kept inactive as the target tone is raw and aggressive; modulation would muddy the sound.
blocks.gap: No specific modulation was requested or implied by the target sound.

blocks.purpose: Kept inactive to maintain the raw, immediate energy of garage rock.
blocks.gap: No specific delay was requested or implied by the target sound.

blocks.purpose: Add a subtle sense of space without losing the raw, dry punch of the garage sound.
blocks.gap: A very slight Room reverb is used to prevent the signal from sounding completely sterile, while avoiding the 'spring reverb' specified in 'avoid'.

alternatives.reason: Could also provide a subtle ambience but might sound too polished for this raw tone.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the generic 4x12 IR for a specific British speaker model to better capture the raw, nasal garage sound.

proposals.recommendedAsset: British tweed/chrome speaker IR (e.g., Celestion Greenback or similar)
proposals.reason: The current 4x12 is too generic; a specific British speaker will enhance the nasal, raw garage tone.
